controls.revocation-control: FAULTED -- REVOCATION_CONTROL revocation=1 tag_after_sweep=0 reissued=1, then SIGPROT si_code 2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG) at addr=pc=0x101dc0, equal to the mc_defect_read address supervise resolved from the ELF independently of the run

why_this_run_exists: the 20260921-cheribsd bundle covers 13 of these 18 cases at revocation ON, but contains NO revocation control: its README cites a PoisonCap mode-0 'matched control', a mode-1 arm that faults, and a bounds control. A bounds control and a PoisonCap differential do not show that CheriBSD's REVOKER sweeps, which is the only thing that makes a temporal completion mean 'the mechanism is active and did not fire'. That is the bar the ffmpeg and memcached readings meet, and this run brings wmem to it. The 5 spatial rows (13-17) additionally had no bundle at all.
control_is_borrowed: ports/memcached/allocators/security-tests/cheribsd/revocation-control.c, unchanged. Borrowing is proven: the ffmpeg pool reading used the same file, and the control exports its probe as a global asm label so one supervisor resolves it regardless of which corpus is under test.
mode_0_is_the_stock_arm: mode 0 is the port's unprotected baseline -- objects are request-bounded and a packet-pool reset revokes nothing -- which is exactly the arm that asks what the SHIPPING temporal mechanism does. Modes 1/2 are the port's own protection and are measured elsewhere.

platform.note: stock CheriBSD purecap built on this host; kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU from releng/26.07-88f39900c329 = pins.env's CHERIBSD_REV. BYTE-IDENTICAL to the vehicle the ffmpeg and memcached readings used. The 20260921 bundle used image 3571a6d2..., a different (PoisonCap-tree) vehicle, so this run also makes the three programs' columns comparable rather than merely all labelled CheriBSD.

supersedes: results/20260921-cheribsd for the stock-CheriBSD question. That bundle is kept: it carries the PoisonCap arms, which this run does not measure.
